note: Hebrew wayya'arikhu habbaddim means the poles "were long" (or "they lengthened"), explaining why their ends were visible; nothing says they were pulled out.
Hebrew beit zevul uses zevul "lofty abode, princely dwelling" (cf. Ugaritic zbl "prince"), not a plain dwelling.

kjv: so that thy children take heed
note: Hebrew raq im "only if" makes the promise conditional; KJV "so that" meant "provided that" in 1611 but now reads as purpose.
Hebrew hasil is a type of locust (the "consumer"), not a caterpillar.

kjv: Let your heart therefore be perfect
mine: Let your hearts be wholly devoted
note: Hebrew shalem means whole, undivided in loyalty; "perfect" now suggests sinlessness.
Hebrew minhah here is the grain offering; "meat" in 1611 meant food in general, and now suggests flesh.
Hebrew levo hamat is best taken as a place name, Lebo of Hamath, the northern boundary town, rather than "the entrance to Hamath."
